title: Velocity entering cylinder 1
description: Essential: Student must correctly calculate v₁ = √(2Ue/m) using work-energy theorem.

title: Motion analysis to cylinder 2
description: Important: Student must describe four distinct phases: acceleration in gap 0→1, uniform motion in cylinder 1, acceleration in gap 1→2, uniform motion in cylinder 2.

title: Cylinder length formula
description: Essential: Student must derive Lₙ = (T/2)√(2nUe/m) by combining vₙ = √(2nUe/m) with half-period travel time.

title: Maximum speed with gap time
description: Important: Student must recognize that maximum speed occurs when cumulative delay equals T/2, preventing further acceleration.

title: Acceleration in gaps
description: Important: Student must calculate acceleration a = Ue/(dm) from electric force and Newton's second law.

title: Gap time consideration
description: Optional: Student may discuss how finite gap transit time causes entry delays into cylinders.

title: Sign error in work-energy
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly handles electron charge sign in potential energy change (Ue not -Ue).

title: Period timing confusion
description: Pitfall: Student uses full period T instead of half-period T/2 for cylinder transit time.

title: Velocity formula misapplication
description: Pitfall: Student uses kinematics v = at instead of work-energy for vₙ, ignoring cumulative energy gain.
